scope: VAL-04 and PERF-02..05; observed samples/source limits, not full benefit or performance acceptance

observed: The repository retains real-model engine cost pilot/rerun records and a 2026-10-24 TS/Rust structural conformance run. The latter uses 12 scenarios across two engines, one pass per cell, and pins a separate vision model.
This takeover separates fixture/implementation tests from benefit claims and has made no paid provider calls.
remaining: Existing cross-engine pilots/conformance are not same-task, same-model, repeated individual-mechanism ablations with correctness/cost/p50/p95/failure distributions.
An approved real-model task budget and frozen VAL-01/02 baseline are still needed before running the paid comparisons. No answer to the pending budget question has been received.
Mechanisms without measured net benefit cannot be declared adopted by these offline test counts.

observed: The app timeline model/projection/measurement cases pass in the 21-case DOM-fixture batch and separate cached history/loading state from view selection.
Native snapshot uses committed projections in a single transaction, with a metadata-only path that omits messages.
remaining: Rust TranscriptPane render still clones the entire lines vector into a Paragraph, and set_transcript rebuilds the formatted transcript. This is not proven visible-window-only rendering.
No 16.7 ms scroll-frame budget distribution or over-budget fraction was measured on large histories.
Native full snapshot materialization and per-event reload costs require a large-history trace; projection-table reads are not automatically constant-time rendering.

observed: Five published 0.3.14 macOS arm64 CLI/TUI/engine starts used one tiny isolated workspace, a new then reused small database, and a zero-delay local provider fixture. Each run made one fixture request; no paid model call.
Composer-visible median is 1615.92 ms (range 1087.84..2140.05); fixture-reply-visible median is 1879.04 ms (range 1351.69..2379.0). Raw samples retain request-arrival timing and collection limits.

Open PR #1583 compares matched Bun 1.4.2 control/feature builds in five interleaved pairs: composer-visible median 472.63 to 339.85 ms (about 28% lower), with identical public TUI/engine and local replies. This is separate from the published-asset startup baseline.
remaining: This small sequential sample does not establish production cold/warm p50/p95, a large-repository/old-database matrix, or distinct input-ready/submit-ready milestones.

The observations do not demonstrate the suggested 500 ms warm-input target. PR #1583 addresses explicit existing project paths through lazy TUI dispatch, but remains unmerged and does not establish the whole startup matrix.
Local fixture reply time is not real provider network latency; terminal capture/poll overhead is included.

observed: Published CLI/TUI/engine and the feature TUI each have eight short idle samples, with per-component RSS, OS CPU moving-average values and cumulative CPU times. All owned sample processes were confirmed exited.

The baseline redraw timer fires every 100 ms while relative timestamp labels change by the minute. Open PR #1581 uses 60-second clock refresh and skips missed ticks; input/engine/resize repaint stays event-driven. Remote 186 Rust TUI tests/fmt/clippy/release build pass.
remaining: These 3.6-second sample windows are not 100 Session switches, long streaming/idle runs or leak/convergence evidence. OS CPU moving averages include prior startup and must not be misread as interval idle CPU.
Broker/LSP/worker were not active in these samples; FD counts were not measured. RSS sums can double-count shared pages.
The timer interval change does not establish a measured 600x CPU benefit and is not yet merged/released.

observed: The actual paused TCP SSE fixture exercises a large payload while a healthy peer and reconnect keep receiving. Native HTTP/ACP tests cover cursor order, slow stdio and independent lease lifetime.
The unconfigured durable event fixture failed through accidental native backend selection; its explicit TS control passes. That environment dependency is retained in checks-clients-replay.txt.
remaining: Rust TUI Bus, transport events and outbound paths use unbounded channels. The selected successful HTTP/stdio cases do not establish bounded UI queues under sustained overload.
The UI loop renders per received event and provides no demonstrated input/cancel/approval priority over event backlog.
Slow-disk/broadcast-lag/large-payload cancellation stress and semantic-equivalent delta batching remain unverified.
